question: is there a screenwriting concentration

body.answer:
Yes. The catalog names a Screenwriting Concentration within the Filmmaking BA, a Bachelor of Arts. It requires FILM 344 WRITING THE SCREENPLAY and FILM 391 TV WRITERS' ROOM. [1][5]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-FILM) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

Ramapo lists Crime and Justice Studies as a minor, not a criminology major. Ramapo lists Crime and Justice Studies as a minor, not a criminology major. question: does ramapo have a creative writing major

body.answer:
No. The catalog lists no bachelor’s major in Creative Writing. It does list a Creative Writing Minor and a Creative Writing Concentration, including a Teacher Education Track with Creative Writing Concentration, within the English & Literary Studies BA. [13] The English and Literary Studies BA offers a Creative Writing concentration and a Creative Writing minor. [9]

**School of Arts, Humanities, and Education Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7365. Email: AHEOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: B-224. [14]

body.answer:
Yes. Photography is a concentration in the Visual Arts BA (Bachelor of Arts). The Visual Arts Minor is also published. [19][1]

The concentration requires ARHT 214 PHOTOGRAPHY CONCEPTS AND HISTORIES and ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY; ARTS 202 BASIC SCULPTURE and ARTS 211 BASIC ART & TECHNOLOGY; and one of ARTS 101 FUNDAMENTALS OF DRAWING or ARTS 201 BASIC PAINTING. [1]

It also requires one upper-level arts elective from the listed choices; three photography electives from ARTS 312 INTERMEDIATE FILM PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 315 MEDIUM AND LARGE FORMAT PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 318 INTERMEDIATE DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 324 DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 328 PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPHY, and ARTS 406 ADVANCED PHOTOGRAPHY; CNTP 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP CONTEMPORARY ARTS; and ARTS 408 SENIOR THESIS EXHIBITION. The page notes: “Complete 1 Additional Required Course from the following list: - 300-level Art History (ARHT) Course” and lists ARHT 204 INTRODUCTION TO GLOBAL ART TRADITIONS and ARHT 245 MASTERPIECES IN WESTERN CIVILIZATION. [1]

ARTS 206 is 4 credits, has no published prerequisites, and carries Gen Ed 18-Culture & Creativity (GECC). [3] ARTS 312 and ARTS 315 are each 4 credits; each requires ARTS 206. [4][6] ARTS 318 is 4 credits and requires ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY. [5] ARTS 406 is 4 credits and requires one of ARTS 312, ARTS 315, ARTS 318, ARTS 324, or ARTS 328. [7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS206) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS312) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS318) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS315) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS406) [19](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

answer:
Yes. Photography is a concentration in the Visual Arts BA (Bachelor of Arts). The Visual Arts Minor is also published. [19][1]

The concentration requires ARHT 214 PHOTOGRAPHY CONCEPTS AND HISTORIES and ARTS 206 BLACK AND WHITE PHOTOGRAPHY; ARTS 202 BASIC SCULPTURE and ARTS 211 BASIC ART & TECHNOLOGY; and one of ARTS 101 FUNDAMENTALS OF DRAWING or ARTS 201 BASIC PAINTING. [1]

It also requires one upper-level arts elective from the listed choices; three photography electives from ARTS 312 INTERMEDIATE FILM PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 315 MEDIUM AND LARGE FORMAT PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 318 INTERMEDIATE DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 324 DOCUMENTARY PHOTOGRAPHY, ARTS 328 PORTRAIT PHOTOGRAPHY, and ARTS 406 ADVANCED PHOTOGRAPHY; CNTP 388 CO-OP/INTERNSHIP CONTEMPORARY ARTS; and ARTS 408 SENIOR THESIS EXHIBITION. The page notes: “Complete 1 Additional Required Course from the following list: - 300-level Art History (ARHT) Course” and lists ARHT 204 INTRODUCTION TO GLOBAL ART TRADITIONS and ARHT 245 MASTERPIECES IN WESTERN CIVILIZATION. [1]

ARTS 206 is 4 credits, has no published prerequisites, and carries Gen Ed 18-Culture & Creativity (GECC). [3] ARTS 312 and ARTS 315 are each 4 credits; each requires ARTS 206. [4][6] ARTS 318 is 4 credits and requires ARTS 207 DIGITAL PHOTOGRAPHY. [5] ARTS 406 is 4 credits and requires one of ARTS 312, ARTS 315, ARTS 318, ARTS 324, or ARTS 328. [7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BA-ARTS) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS206) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS312) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS318) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS315) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/ARTS406) [19](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

body.answer:
The Psychology BA, a Bachelor of Arts major, has no total credit count stated in its catalog requirements; the requirements list courses, and I can’t add them up [1]. The Registrar says each program has different credit requirements and advises reviewing the number of classes and credits with your adviser [7]. Contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office for the major requirements [2].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [15]
- **School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7625; (201) 684-7562. Email: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-431. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/sssw/psychology/faqs/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how many credits to graduate w a nursing degree

body.answer:
Undergraduate Nursing degrees (Generic BSN, Accelerated BSN, and RN to BSN) require at least 128 credits to graduate. You must complete at least 48 credits at Ramapo, including your final 32 credits in residence, and at least half of the credits for your major at Ramapo. Nursing majors must maintain a 2.3 GPA. [6][7] The Registrar says a minimum of 32 credits must be completed at Ramapo, but the newer graduation page requires 48. [5][6]

The Nursing MSN’s catalog requirements list courses but do not give a total credit count. [1] The Nursing Generic BSN’s catalog requirements likewise list courses without a program total. [2] Review the number of classes and credits with your adviser; contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising). [5]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [14]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [14]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MSN-NURM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
Undergraduate Nursing degrees (Generic BSN, Accelerated BSN, and RN to BSN) require at least 128 credits to graduate. You must complete at least 48 credits at Ramapo, including your final 32 credits in residence, and at least half of the credits for your major at Ramapo. Nursing majors must maintain a 2.3 GPA. [6][7] The Registrar says a minimum of 32 credits must be completed at Ramapo, but the newer graduation page requires 48. [5][6]

The Nursing MSN’s catalog requirements list courses but do not give a total credit count. [1] The Nursing Generic BSN’s catalog requirements likewise list courses without a program total. [2] Review the number of classes and credits with your adviser; contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising). [5]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [14]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [14]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MSN-NURM) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i use the photo lighting studio if im not in a photo class

body.answer:
Not generally. Use is restricted to students in specified photography courses, but other CA courses may be approved case by case; Visual Arts majors and students previously trained on the studio equipment may also use it. Students should make reservations for the Lighting Studio (BC 140A). [1][4]

**Photography Lab**: Phone: (201) 684-7235. Email: photolab@ramapo.edu. Location: Berrie Center 135. Eva Fazzari, Photography Lab Supervisor: Berrie Center 139; Lighting Studio: BC-140A. [33]

question: whats the grad certificate in business foundations n is it online

body.answer:
The Anisfield School of Business Graduate Certificate in Business Foundations is designed for students who are not business majors and want to learn business fundamentals; it can also be a path to an MBA. [2] It provides graduate-level foundational knowledge in Accounting, Economics, Marketing, Finance, Management, and Business Statistics. [1] The certificate requires six 2-credit courses: ACCT 510 FOUNDATIONS OF ACCOUNTING, BADM 510 FOUNDATION STATS FOR BUSINESS, ECON 510 FOUNDATIONS OF ECONOMICS, FINC 510 FOUNDATIONS OF FINANCE, MGMT 510 FOUNDATIONS OF MANAGEMENT, and MKTG 510 FOUNDATIONS OF MARKETING. [1] All classes are taken entirely online; the courses are offered online in both fall and spring semesters. [4][5] It can be completed in one semester. [5]

- **Anisfield School of Business**: Phone: Phone (201) 684-7379; Phone (201) 684-7380; Phone (201) 684-7378; Fax (201) 684-7957. Email: asb@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-333. [15]
- **Ramapo College Foundation**: Phone: (201) 684-6819. Institutional Advancement: Birch Mansion. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-GCR-BUFN) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb/graduate-certificate-in-business-foundations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb/graduate-certificate-in-business-foundations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/asb/graduate-certificate-in-business-foundations/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

IGG can also be used to help exonerate the wrongfully convicted. Relying on informed consent and publicly available information, IGG begins with genetic genealogy databases that allow users to choose whether to make their DNA profiles available for IGG searching. First, a DNA profile derived from a biological sample belonging either to a perpetrator or an unidentified individual—either is referred to as the Subject—is uploaded to the databases. From those databases, IGG practitioners use statistical measures of relatedness based on amounts of shared DNA to determine likely relationships between the Subject and users in the databases. The bulk of IGG, however, relies on traditional genealogy – combing through public records to fill out the family tree belonging to the Subject in order to narrow in on that individual’s likely place in the tree. The IGG Bootcamp is a week-long summer program on Ramapo’s campus where students practice their skills through intensive, focused casework in the secure Investigative Genetic Genealogy Lab. It also offers dynamic learning opportunities and helps build teamwork and professional connections. [2]

Students who complete the Ramapo College IGG Certificate Program may apply; up to 15 participants will be accepted. [2] The next Bootcamp is July 6–9, 2027. It costs $2,000, including an on-campus dorm room and meals as listed on the Bootcamp page. [2]

**Investigative Genetic Genealogy Center**: Email: igg@ramapo.edu. [23]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/igg/bootcamp/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

answer:
The IGG Bootcamp is a week-long summer program on Ramapo’s campus where students practice their skills through intensive, focused casework in the secure Investigative Genetic Genealogy Lab. It also offers dynamic learning opportunities and helps build teamwork and professional connections. [2]

Students who complete the Ramapo College IGG Certificate Program may apply; up to 15 participants will be accepted. [2] The next Bootcamp is July 6–9, 2027. It costs $2,000, including an on-campus dorm room and meals as listed on the Bootcamp page. [2]

**Investigative Genetic Genealogy Center**: Email: igg@ramapo.edu. [23]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/igg/bootcamp/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is bridging the gap a real class n when does it meet

body.answer:
Yes. CIVL 201, “BRIDGING THE GAP: SKILLS FOR INTERCULTURAL DIALOGUE,” is a 2-credit course; no prerequisites are published. [1] The RCNJ Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies page lists Jacob Ari Labendz and says the BtG course meets Tuesdays, 9:55–11:35 am, Spring Semester 2027. [2] For more information, contact Dr. Jacob Ari Labendz at holgen@ramapo.edu. [2]

**RCNJ Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies**: Phone: (201) 684-7409. Email: holgen@ramapo.edu. Office: LC-216. [14]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CIVL201) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/holocaust/for-students/btg/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: where do nursing students do clinicals

body.answer:
The Nursing Programs Office says accelerated and generic nursing students spend much of their clinical time at The Valley Hospital. Other affiliates include St. Joseph’s Regional Medical Center, Hackensack Meridian Health Network, New Bridge Medical Center, Valley Home Care, Township of Garfield, Bergen County Department of Public Health, and other local community agencies. Students provide their own transportation to clinical sites. [7][8] The accelerated FAQ says placements are scheduled in NJ within a 60 minute radius of campus. [11]

- **Nursing Programs Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7749. Location: Adler Center for Nursing Excellence 215. [15]
- **Transportation Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: shuttle@ramapo.edu. [15]

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/clinical-unique-experiences/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/bsn-generic/clinical-unique-experiences/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/faqs/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: applying to the accelerated nursing program do i need to send transcripts if i went to ramapo

body.answer:
If you are a graduating Ramapo College student or alum, you do not need to submit your transcripts. You only need to submit and upload the following to your application: One letter of recommendation, current resume, and ATI TEAS Exam Results. [5] Current or former Ramapo students who have not completed a non-Nursing Bachelor’s or Associate’s Degree at Ramapo or elsewhere are not eligible for the Accelerated BSN Program at this time. [6]

question: is there a nursing honor society

body.answer:
Yes. Sigma Theta Tau International, Ramapo College chapter, is the nursing honor society. It recognizes students with outstanding achievements in nursing; students are invited to apply once they earn a GPA in the Nursing sequence. [14]

**Nursing Programs Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7749. Location: Adler Center for Nursing Excellence 215. [26]

question: does the ms in accounting get me to 150 credits for the cpa

body.answer:
Yes. The Accounting MS is designed to bring you to 150 credits required to sit for the CPA exam when combined with an undergraduate degree [1]. The program consists of 30 credits and is designed to build upon an undergraduate degree in accounting to meet the 150-credit requirement for New Jersey CPA certification [2].

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [13]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MS-MSAC) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/msac/faqs/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how long does the mba take if i work full time

body.answer:
Ramapo’s MBA page says students with “Advanced Standing” can finish in as little as 12 months; students without it can finish in as little as 18 months. Students with a business undergraduate degree are automatically granted “Advanced Standing.” The page says enrollees choose their pace to suit their personal and professional needs, but does not give a separate timeline for working full time. [2]

answer:
Ramapo’s MBA page says students with “Advanced Standing” can finish in as little as 12 months; students without it can finish in as little as 18 months. Students with a business undergraduate degree are automatically granted “Advanced Standing.” The page says enrollees choose their pace to suit their personal and professional needs, but does not give a separate timeline for working full time. [2]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [14]

question: can i pick my own practicum site for social work

body.answer:
You can discuss choosing your own practicum site with the Director of Practicum Education. Sites must meet certain criteria and be approved by the Practicum Education Department. [3]

For BSW placements, the process considers your interests, location, appropriate assignments, and supervision; the college sends you to one agency at a time for an interview, so you should not ask to interview at several agencies and then expect to pick one. [4][5][7] Contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office for guidance. [3]

answer:
You can discuss choosing your own practicum site with the Director of Practicum Education. Sites must meet certain criteria and be approved by the Practicum Education Department. [3]

For BSW placements, the process considers your interests, location, appropriate assignments, and supervision; the college sends you to one agency at a time for an interview, so you should not ask to interview at several agencies and then expect to pick one. [4][5][7] Contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office for guidance. [3]

**School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7625; (201) 684-7562. Email: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu. Office: ASB-431. [15]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/social-work/msw/faqs/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/social-work/bsw/practicum-education/theory-and-practice/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/social-work/bsw/practicum-education/agencies-communities/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/social-work/bsw/practicum-education/agencies-communities/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
